prompts.title: Explain the full TVA workflow
prompts.description: HEADWATER through Georgia Tech, with each handoff in view.
prompts.livePrompt: Explain our TVA water–energy workflow across the whole ELF network: HEADWATER precipitation, air-temperature and runoff forecasts; physical reconstruction and high-resolution downscaling; Yang’s LSTM water-availability model; and Georgia Tech economic assessment. Describe each team’s inputs, outputs and current integration status. Explain the optional TRITON hydraulics and RiTHyMs water-temperature paths when plant analysis requires them. Use read-only inspection and planning only. Identify missing skills, files or runtime prerequisites. Do not submit jobs, train, install software, change settings or fabricate outputs.
prompts.recordedAnswer:
The project has four main stages.

1. HEADWATER supplies precipitation, air-temperature and runoff forecasts for the TVA region. The TRITON discussion describes a 25 km residual/probability-map handoff.
2. Reconstruction and downscaling use forecast maps and historical references to form physical scenarios, with 4 km intermediate and 1 km target grids.
3. Yang’s LSTM estimates weekly water availability at TVA ELF sites from prepared basin forcing and static attributes. Recorded model results are available in this workspace.
4. Georgia Tech receives plant water records and combines them with plant/economic data to assess generation, cost and risk. Those metrics and the partner interface still need agreement.

TRITON can add hydraulic detail, and RiTHyMs can supply water temperature near plants. These are additional paths where the plant handoff needs them. VISTA orchestrates scientific tools and records their evidence. The workflow diagram describes the project design; the Skills view shows what is actually loaded.

prompts.title: Explore all 52 TVA ELF sites
prompts.description: Study the full network and understand the reference quantities.
prompts.livePrompt: Review the TVA network for ELF01 through ELF52 using the supplied ELF site inventory and network reference maps. Explain the site coverage and distinguish Estimated Local Flow reference quantities from total upstream inflow. Identify which selected sites have prepared inputs and recorded or live predictions, and what remains to run the whole network. Do not sum overlapping or allocated site flows. Use read-only inspection and planning only. Identify missing skills, files or runtime prerequisites. Do not submit jobs, train, install software, change settings or fabricate outputs.
prompts.recordedAnswer:
The TVA network covers ELF01 through ELF52. ELF stands for Estimated Local Flow. Use the full-network map, site selector and original map/schematic references to inspect the site context.

A site’s ELF reference may represent local, incremental or allocated flow. Confirm that definition before calling the quantity plant inflow or adding it to another site. The LSTM produces site-specific predictions; overlapping reference quantities should not be summed into a network total. Recorded examples and any live result must retain their own site IDs, dates and provenance.

prompts.recordedAnswer:
The HEADWATER handoff supplies precipitation, air temperature and runoff. The TRITON discussion labels the incoming fields as residual/probability maps at 25 km. Downstream models need physical scenarios, so the handoff must specify the historical reference used for reconstruction.

Retain grid/coordinate metadata, variable definitions, units, forecast issue time, valid time and member IDs. The included recorded LSTM examples do not demonstrate a live HEADWATER forecast ingestion.

prompts.title: Plan high-resolution downscaling
prompts.description: Follow the regional fields to the 1 km target.
prompts.livePrompt: Prepare the TVA reconstruction and downscaling plan using HEADWATER forecast maps and historical reference maps. The project slides name a 4 km intermediate grid and 1 km target. Identify the available downscaling implementation or skill, its input/output grids, precipitation and temperature fields, runoff treatment, physical units and time/member metadata. Explain aggregation from high-resolution grids into the forcing regions required by Yang’s LSTM. Use read-only inspection and planning only. Identify missing skills, files or runtime prerequisites. Do not submit jobs, train, install software, change settings or fabricate outputs.
prompts.recordedAnswer:
Reconstruction combines the forecast maps with historical reference maps to obtain physical scenarios. The project discussion then targets high-resolution TVA fields, with 4 km intermediate and 1 km target grids.

Before the LSTM stage, those gridded fields must satisfy the model’s basin-week forcing contract. Preserve the variable definitions, units and time/member identities during downscaling and spatial aggregation. The target grid in the slides is a design target; it does not establish that a downscaling skill is installed.

prompts.title: Prepare the LSTM inference plan
prompts.description: Validate the selected sites and saved-model inputs first.
prompts.livePrompt: Prepare an inference plan for Yang’s saved TVA LSTM across the selected ELF sites, with the whole ELF01–ELF52 network as the intended study scope. Use the loaded TVA inference skill. Identify the selected model, matched basin-week CSV/metadata, twelve preceding weeks plus each target week, static attributes, frozen checkpoint, Python environment and compatible compute resource. Explain output units and each site’s ELF meaning. Show the exact proposed job settings and expected artifacts, then wait for my explicit confirmation before submission. Use read-only inspection and planning only. Identify missing skills, files or runtime prerequisites. Do not submit jobs, train, install software, change settings or fabricate outputs.
prompts.recordedAnswer:
Yang’s LSTM uses prepared basin-week precipitation, temperature and runoff, plus the static attributes required by the chosen model. A target week uses its forcing together with twelve preceding weeks of history. This is a thirteen-week input window, rather than a thirteen-week forecast lead.

The existing model outputs weekly ELF reference quantities and can retain predictions, provenance and input-quality flags. Select sites in the network/evidence views to inspect the recorded sample. A live plan must verify the loaded skill, matched CSV/metadata/model, frozen checkpoint and accessible compute environment before submission.

prompts.title: Explain hydraulics and water temperature
prompts.description: How TRITON and RiTHyMs support plant records.
prompts.livePrompt: Describe the optional plant-impact paths in TRITON_discussion: TRITON for hydraulics and RiTHyMs for river temperature. Check which matching skills are loaded. Explain terrain, roughness, upstream Q/runoff and boundary conditions for TRITON, and the extraction needed to turn H and QX/QY into depth, stage and section discharge. Explain meteorology/flow/attributes for RiTHyMs, and keep the later reservoir/CE-QUAL-W2 path separate. Relate the outputs to Yang’s LSTM and the plant data interface. Use read-only inspection and planning only. Identify missing skills, files or runtime prerequisites. Do not submit jobs, train, install software, change settings or fabricate outputs.
prompts.recordedAnswer:
The plant handoff may need more than a weekly water-availability quantity. TRITON can add hydraulic information using runoff or upstream discharge, terrain, roughness and initial/boundary conditions. Its H and QX/QY outputs require appropriate extraction to report depth, stage and section discharge.

RiTHyMs uses meteorology, suitable flow and site/reach attributes to estimate river water temperature in °C. The discussion leaves reservoir setup and a CE-QUAL-W2 reservoir/release-temperature path for later work. These optional models complement the LSTM water-availability stage. The slides explicitly leave TRITON TVA readiness, routing needs and an agentic skill unresolved.

prompts.title: Prepare Georgia Tech’s data handoff
prompts.description: Plant water records, assumptions and economic metrics.
prompts.livePrompt: Prepare the Georgia Tech economic-assessment handoff for the TVA case. Draft a data contract using plant/site mapping, water quantity with its physical definition and units, water temperature when required, daily/weekly timing, forecast issue/member IDs, quality flags and provenance, plus optional hydraulic depth/stage/section discharge. Identify partner-supplied plant/economic inputs and which generation, cost and risk metrics still require agreement. Do not infer economic impacts from an LSTM prediction without the partner model and assumptions. Use read-only inspection and planning only. Identify missing skills, files or runtime prerequisites. Do not submit jobs, train, install software, change settings or fabricate outputs.
prompts.recordedAnswer:
Georgia Tech is responsible for economic assessment. The TRITON discussion sends daily/weekly plant water records, site/plant IDs, units and quality flags to the partner, with water temperature and optional hydraulics when the assessment needs them.

Georgia Tech combines those records with plant/economic data to evaluate generation, cost and risk. The metrics still need agreement. The handoff should preserve forecast timing/member IDs and scientific provenance, and confirm how each ELF site quantity maps to a plant. The workspace does not create economic estimates from the recorded LSTM chart alone.
